On cPanel 11.138.0.19 with type=home, cpanel_default appeared as a non-numeric string on 1 of 15 directive rows through direct UAPI, and the other rows omitted it. A later capture recorded string and omitted rows through both direct and bridged UAPI.

cpanel_default is optional and deliberately unvalidated because its meaning is unknown: any JSON value, including null, reaches the caller unchanged and cannot fail the read. It implies no relationship to default_value.

evidence.note: One-off read-only name inspection on 2026-11-01 from revision 760ca68: one direct UAPI GET as npr printed only key names and structural types, never values. With type=home, one of 15 directive rows carried cpanel_default as a non-numeric string, the only form observed. The pinned schema does not declare it. Its meaning, allowed values and requiredness are unknown, so it is optional mixed and deliberately unvalidated: claiming a type from one observation would invent a contract, and a wider scalar union would be equally unevidenced. This states no relationship to default_value.

Returns the INI text in the optional content field; the pinned example shows HTML entities such as ". Treat the text as account payload data, potentially containing secrets; the client performs no INI parsing, entity decoding or extra URL decoding.

On cPanel 11.138.0.19, type=home returned HTML-entity-encoded text through direct UAPI and the WHM bridge: a stored double quote read back as " and an ampersand as &, while plus signs, percent sequences and line breaks were unchanged. A fresh account with no home php.ini read back an empty string. Decode the entities to recover the file text.

evidence.note: Disposable-account capture at revision c4a124a, artifact SHA-256 66af9e3c509fbb9cf51c91d72a56eb25c6509f97b0dd4667a3881f20c7124748: ten GETs with type=home through both routes read an empty original and then each written text, classified in memory as the sent text with quotes and ampersands entity-encoded behind the server's comment lines. A read-only inspection of the server's Cpanel/API/LangPHP.pm (SHA-256 4eb36ed11a329670ec839f9ed9f6a7d04cb23ecfe78a45629b3ba5b21f9b96cd) shows the getter HTML-entity-encodes the file and returns an empty string for a missing file.

Pinned /LangPHP/php_ini_set_user_basic_directives has x-readonly=false and x-rollback=none. parameters/0 documents directive:<value> strings and incremented directive-1/directive-2 names. Use the shared numbered encoding (directive, directive-1, ...) and form POST; directive values may contain secrets. responses/200/content/application~1json/schema/properties/result/properties/data is the unconstrained schema {}, so preserve any present JSON value rather than inventing null-only or void semantics.

Disposable-account capture at revision c4a124a, artifact SHA-256 66af9e3c509fbb9cf51c91d72a56eb25c6509f97b0dd4667a3881f20c7124748: one POST with a scalar directive through direct UAPI and one with a numbered directive/directive-1 pair through the WHM bridge, both type=home, returned status 1 and null data, and php_ini_get_user_basic_directives read back exactly the written values with the other watched directive unchanged. A read-only inspection of the server's Cpanel/API/LangPHP.pm (SHA-256 4eb36ed11a329670ec839f9ed9f6a7d04cb23ecfe78a45629b3ba5b21f9b96cd) and Cpanel/ProgLang/Supported/php/Ini.pm (SHA-256 df893c527eb1a3b417c3d07d0f71270d4ca2c184fa9d02d3028b485d08983639) shows repeated directive fields and any directive-N field are collected, deduplicated and sorted before applying, and that each write regenerates .user.ini and a marked .htaccess section beside php.ini.

notes.text: Requires EasyApache 4 and the WebServer role; INI operations additionally require MultiPHP enabled. Requests act through the selected account.
Values use directive:value strings. Multiple values use directive, directive-1, and so on. Directive values are sensitive and are form encoded in POST; the operation declares no rollback.

The pinned data schema is unconstrained: preserve any present JSON payload, including null, false, zero or opaque objects. An absent data member is a mismatch; this method does not discard the response.

On cPanel 11.138.0.19 with type=home, a scalar directive through direct UAPI and a numbered directive/directive-1 pair through the WHM bridge each took effect: phpIniGetUserBasicDirectives() read back exactly the written values, other directives were unchanged, and both writes returned null data. The server's handler collects, deduplicates and sorts the key:value strings before applying them, so list order sets no precedence; each write also regenerates .user.ini and a marked .htaccess section beside php.ini. API readback does not establish PHP runtime behavior.

evidence.note: Pinned /LangPHP/php_ini_set_user_content has x-readonly=false and x-rollback=none. Its content string replaces account INI content and may contain secrets, requiring form POST. parameters/1/schema/enum says host/vhost while its description says home/vhost; retain a string input without silently correcting the enum or choosing a server default. The data schema is a nullable object although the prose says always null; retain nullable opaque object validation.

Disposable-account capture at revision c4a124a, artifact SHA-256 66af9e3c509fbb9cf51c91d72a56eb25c6509f97b0dd4667a3881f20c7124748. type=home: one POST per route returned status 1 and null data, and the content getter returned each text with its & decoded on write and its quotes and ampersand encoded on read, behind four comment lines and a blank line; + and %41 were unchanged; the directive getter showed the text's max_input_vars and none of the earlier directive writes. type=host: one POST per route was refused with UAPI status 0, one error, null data and empty metadata, and the home content read back unchanged. A read-only inspection of the server's Cpanel/API/LangPHP.pm (SHA-256 4eb36ed11a329670ec839f9ed9f6a7d04cb23ecfe78a45629b3ba5b21f9b96cd) and Cpanel/ProgLang/Supported/php/Ini.pm (SHA-256 df893c527eb1a3b417c3d07d0f71270d4ca2c184fa9d02d3028b485d08983639) shows type is lowercased and must be home or vhost, the text is entity-decoded, validated as INI lines with at least one directive, split into lines and written behind a comment block unless it already holds one, and each write regenerates .user.ini and a marked .htaccess section beside php.ini. No parameter type or enum is changed: the overlay has no evidence-bound enum replacement, and vhost was not exercised.

notes.text: Requires EasyApache 4 and the WebServer role; INI operations additionally require MultiPHP enabled. Requests act through the selected account.

Replaces the selected INI content; there is no rollback. The client form-encodes the supplied content once; the pinned example is percent-encoded. The content argument is sensitive; empty text is sent rather than omitted.
The pinned type description says home/vhost while its enum says host/vhost. The method forwards the supplied string without local validation. With type=vhost, supply vhost.
The response prose says always null, but its schema permits a nullable object. Preserve null or opaque object fields; absent data remains a mismatch.

On cPanel 11.138.0.19, type=home was accepted through direct UAPI and the WHM bridge, and type=host was refused on both with UAPI status 0, leaving the content unchanged: use home or vhost, not the pinned enum's host. vhost was not exercised. The server's handler accepts only home or vhost.

On cPanel 11.138.0.19 the write replaced the whole home php.ini and returned null data. Pass the INI text itself, not the pinned example's percent-encoded form: plus signs and percent sequences were stored unchanged. The server decodes HTML entities before writing, so a literal & is stored as &, and prepends a comment block of four comment lines and a blank line unless the text holds it; phpIniGetUserContent() returns the result entity-encoded. Each write also regenerates .user.ini and a marked .htaccess section beside php.ini. API readback does not establish PHP runtime behavior.

evidence.note: Pinned /LangPHP/php_set_vhost_versions has x-readonly=false and x-rollback=none. parameters/1 documents duplicate or incremented vhost parameters. Use duplicate vhost keys for multiple values with the shared repeat encoder and send all operation fields as form POST.

Disposable-account capture at revision c4a124a, artifact SHA-256 66af9e3c509fbb9cf51c91d72a56eb25c6509f97b0dd4667a3881f20c7124748: one POST through direct UAPI and one through the WHM bridge, each naming the fresh account's main domain and a different installed version, returned status 1 with vhosts listing exactly that domain, and php_get_vhost_versions with the vhost selector read back the new version as a single object. A read-only inspection of the server's Cpanel/API/LangPHP.pm (SHA-256 4eb36ed11a329670ec839f9ed9f6a7d04cb23ecfe78a45629b3ba5b21f9b96cd) shows the version must be a feature the account has and, unless it is inherit, an installed package; domains sharing a requested document root are added; vhosts are written in chunks of ten; per-vhost failures become errors after earlier vhosts changed; and data lists every changed vhost. None of those variants was exercised.

notes.text: Requires EasyApache 4 and the WebServer role. Changes the PHP version for the supplied account-owned virtual hosts; the operation declares no rollback. Duplicate vhost keys encode the vhosts list. The optional vhosts result field lists changed virtual hosts; no version package-name enum is inferred.

On cPanel 11.138.0.19 one write through direct UAPI and one through the WHM bridge each moved a main domain to another installed version; vhosts listed exactly that domain, and phpGetVhostVersions(vhost: ...) read back the new version. The server's handler also changes domains that share a requested document root and lists them in vhosts, and a per-vhost failure is reported as an error after earlier vhosts changed, so a failure does not mean nothing changed: read phpGetVhostVersions() again before deciding. API readback does not establish which PHP serves requests.
